Source Code & Dev Tools
 GitHub
Back up your entire GitHub organization — repositories, CI/CD pipelines, organization settings, and compliance audit logs.
 Bitbucket
Back up Bitbucket repositories, branches, and pull requests across your workspace.
 GitLab
Back up GitLab groups, projects, merge requests, issues, CI/CD configuration, and audit logs.
 Azure DevOps
Back up Azure DevOps repositories, pipelines, work items, boards, and organization settings.
Collaboration & Productivity
 Microsoft 365
Back up Exchange mailboxes, SharePoint sites, OneDrive files, and Teams data.
 SharePoint
Back up SharePoint sites, libraries, lists, and page content across tenants.
 Google Workspace
Protect your Gmail, Drives, Calendar, Contacts and more against accidental deletion, ransomware, and retention gaps.
 Box
Back up cloud files, documents, and folder structures with Box.
 Confluence
Back up Confluence Cloud spaces, pages, blog posts, comments, attachments, and labels.
 Jira
Backup and granular restore for Jira Cloud projects, issues, attachments, worklogs, boards, and sprints.
Business Applications
 Microsoft Power Platform
Back up Power BI, Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power Pages.
 Microsoft Dynamics 365
Protect Microsoft Dataverse and Dynamics 365 data
 Salesforce
Back up Salesforce CRM records, configurations, and metadata.
Identity & Directory
 Okta Workforce Identity Cloud
Identity-aware backup & recovery for users, groups, authentication policies, applications, and federations.
 Google Identity Protection
Protect identities across Google Workspace, Cloud Identity, and GCP IAM.
 Microsoft Entra ID
Back up Entra ID users, groups, app registrations, and conditional access policies.

Recover individual issues, attachments, projects, boards, or sprints to a point-in-time well beyond Atlassian’s 30/60-day trash window.

Requirements apply before connecting
Before you connect
    Express Recommended
    Authorize via GitHub — no credential management required
    Zero-credential management
    Auto-token refresh
    Minimal permission scopes
    GitHub best practices
    Veeam installs the application user automatically when you test the connection — no manual setup required.
    Admin permissions required
    The person authorizing needs Entra ID Application Administrator (or Global Admin) and ADO Project Collection Administrator. Without PCA, the OAuth step still succeeds — you'll add the Service Principal manually after. View detailed steps.
    A GitHub authorization window will open. You'll be redirected back automatically.
    Waiting for GitHub authorization…
    Connected to “securiti-devops”
    Access: ALL repositories
    Manual
    Provide a GitHub App Client ID and Client Secret
    Create an Entra ID app registration in your Azure Portal, assign the required permissions, then enter the credentials here.
    Entra ID admin required
    An Entra ID Application Administrator (or Global Admin) must create the app registration and provide these credentials. The Entra admin doesn't need to be the same person setting up this connection.
    The full URL of your Azure DevOps organization.
    Credential Type
    Certificate
    Upload the public X.509 certificate (.cer) you registered on the Entra app. The matching private key is generated and held by Veeam — you don't upload it here.
    Drag & drop your .cer file here
    or browse to select a file
    The public X.509 certificate. Same file uploaded to the Entra app registration.
    Certificate
    Upload the PKCS#12 (.pfx) bundle that contains both the public certificate and private key. Veeam extracts both internally — only the public certificate is transmitted to Entra.
    Drag & drop your .pfx file here
    or browse to select a file
    PKCS#12 file containing both the public certificate and private key. Stored encrypted at rest. Only the public certificate is transmitted to Entra.
    Required because you indicated the .pfx is passphrase-protected. Stored encrypted at rest.
    Stored encrypted at rest. Never logged or transmitted in plaintext.
    Use a certificate for production
    Client secrets are permitted for development and test environments only. Production deployments must use certificate-based authentication — secrets expire (Entra ID enforces a 2-year maximum), and rotation gaps risk failed backups.
    Paste this URL into your OAuth app’s callback settings.
    Your OAuth app must have the Phase 1 Jira API and Jira Software API scopes added before connecting. View the required scopes →
    Service account credential
    Upload the JSON key of the Google Cloud service account you authorized for domain-wide delegation. The key contains the account's identity and key pair — no separate client ID or secret is needed.
    Drag & drop your service account key file here (.json or .p12)
    or browse to select a file
    Downloaded from the Google Cloud console when you created the service account key — JSON (recommended) or P12. Stored encrypted at rest; never logged.
    The Super Admin the service account impersonates under domain-wide delegation. Must match an active Super Admin in your Workspace domain.
    Veeam generates the keypair and keeps the private key encrypted — it is shown only once.
    Add this key to your app under General → Public Keys → Add. The next step verifies the key and scopes.
    Found in the Google Cloud console under IAM & Admin → Settings. The service account's IAM roles must be granted at this organization node.
    The Super Admin the service account impersonates under domain-wide delegation. Must match an active Super Admin in your Workspace domain.
    Service account credential
    Upload the JSON key of the Google Cloud service account you authorized for domain-wide delegation. The key contains the account's identity and key pair — no separate client ID or secret is needed.
    Drag & drop your service account key file here (.json or .p12)
    or browse to select a file
    Downloaded from the Google Cloud console when you created the service account key — JSON (recommended) or P12. Stored encrypted at rest; never logged.
